request.spec:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Rates can now have a to-date, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What a to-date does**
- When you set a rate you can give a to-date as well as a from-date. A to-date earlier than the from-date is refused: the form shows `rate-form-error`, and the server also rejects it, so nothing is saved or audited. Each rate row now shows its to-date (`rate-to`).
- The `RATE_SET` audit line gets ` to=<date>` at the end when a to-date was given.
- The rate a claim would use is still the one with the latest from-date on or before the claim's date. If that rate has ended by then, the claim's due is n/a. An older rate does not come back into force once a later one ends. The server (`RateRepository.on`) and the screen (`rateOn` in `rates.ts`) apply this same rule, so totals, rollups, statements, overdue figures, the late charge and "in force today" all follow it.
- New migration `V30__rate_to.sql` adds a `to_date` column to the rate table.

**A behaviour change to check:** to make "a statement binds n/a" work, a stated claim now keeps n/a even after a rate is set later. Before, a claim stated with no figure went back to being worked out from the current rate (unless it was PENDING). I changed this in `Dues.figure` and the front-end `claimDue`, and the three other scenarios in the spec still pass with it.

A to-date with no from-date is allowed, meaning the rate runs from the beginning of time to that date.
